items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: I also have worked with the band called Roots... and Buster and George Kape, or I’m sorry, Kirk Lightsey.

ctx.x: What’s the best — I don’t know if you can think of this quite offhand, but what’s one of the best musical situations that you’ve been involved in so far?

One of the best? Oh there are a few. Well the one with McCoy is great. For me it’s great. I’m in a quartet situation so there’s a lot of freedom and it’s, again, playing with McCoy. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

This is great. This is one of the best right now. Outside of what I do myself, I think this is probably my favorite thing right now. And I love playing with my father when we do that. I also have worked with the band called Roots, which is like a saxophone quartet with a rhythm section. Actually the original band was great, it originally was Don Pullen on piano, we had Buster Williams on bass and we had Idris Muhammad in the rhythm section. Now it’s Ed Thigpen, which he’s absolutely wonderful drummer, and Buster…
